summary: This bill amends 49 U.S.C. §§ 5314 and 5339 to let transit agencies use up to 10% of Bus and Bus Facilities Program grants for workforce development and training instead of limiting that use to 5% and only for zero-emission projects.

scores.thoughts: The bill reallocates a portion (up to 10%) of existing section 5339 bus grants toward workforce development and training but does not authorize new appropriations or change overall spending levels. It therefore has no net effect on the size of government spending.
The bill contains no tax provisions of any kind.
No provisions relate to healthcare delivery, coverage, or markets.
No provisions address firearms or gun regulations.
No provisions address immigration, visas, or border policy.
No provisions address reproductive health or abortion access.
No provisions address military or defense spending.

The bill removes the prior linkage between workforce-training funds and zero-emission-vehicle transition plans, modestly broadening allowable uses away from an emissions-focused requirement. This produces a small shift away from environmental targeting.
No provisions affect welfare programs, food assistance, or means-tested benefits.
Workforce training is mentioned, but the bill is narrowly limited to transit-agency employees and does not engage federal education policy or school funding.
No provisions address controlled substances or drug enforcement.
No provisions address policing, sentencing, or criminal-justice reform.
No provisions address tariffs, trade agreements, or import policy.
The bill does not alter revenue or outlays in a way that affects deficits or debt trajectory.
No provisions address LGBTQ protections or related civil-rights measures.
No provisions address foreign assistance.
No provisions address voting access or election administration.
No provisions address technology regulation or data privacy.

The bill expands the share of transit capital grants that may be spent on workforce training for bus operators and maintenance staff, directly supporting skill development for a largely unionized public-transit workforce. This constitutes a modest pro-labor measure.
No provisions address religious exemptions or anti-discrimination rules.
